title: fix(metadata-protocol)!: a delete naming one package keeps the item's other rows registered, and a package-less draft save of an item two packages hold is refused 409
body:
Fixes #23297
Clause-②: yes (narrowing)

## What this does

Three package-axis gaps that the review of PR #23290 left open in `packages/metadata-protocol`. Each was measured before the fix (item 1 on a booted showcase), pinned, and ablated.

**1. The registry heal after a delete that names one package.** `restoreArtifactRegistryView` now asks the store first. If a row of the item is still stored at the address after the delete (the environment's active rows, canonical type, the member, any package), that row is registered again through `applyRegistryWriteThrough`, in the boot hydration's order and with its sealed-object skip, and nothing is retired. For an `object`, the registry keeps one owner per name (ADR-0029 D3). So when the registered owner is the deleted row's package and no code package ships the name, that owner is unregistered first, and the remaining row can then take the name. The existing extender guard and warning are kept. Deleting the last row still retires the item.

- Before (booted showcase, SQLite, `origin/main` `6eb6f7d65`): after `PUT /api/v1/meta/object/qa_probe_gadget?package=com.qa.p`, a `PUT` with `?package=com.qa.q`, then `DELETE ...?package=com.qa.p`, the receipt said "it still exists: its row bound to package 'com.qa.q' remains". `GET /api/v1/meta/object/qa_probe_gadget` answered 200 with Q's row. `GET` and `POST /api/v1/data/qa_probe_gadget` answered `404 OBJECT_NOT_FOUND`, still 404 after a list call. The dev log showed `Removed overlay entry` and `Unregistered object ... owner com.qa.p`.
- After (same sequence, rebuilt `dist`): the data door answers `GET 200` and `POST 201`.

**2. A draft save that names no package, of an item two packages hold.** `SysMetadataRepository.resolveWriteHead` used to read one active row with a package-agnostic `findOne` for the draft inheritance (#11087). It now reads every active row of the address.

- Rows bound to one package: the draft inherits that package in any storage order. A package-less row beside it is not a second package, the rule the direct save follows since #23165.
- Rows bound to two or more packages: the resolution names no package. `put` refuses before anything is written, with `409 RESOURCE_CONFLICT` and the `?package=` remedy, which is the same refusal the direct save and the delete answer. `headAt` answers the package-unbound draft key, so a draft read's `version` never names a package picked by storage order.
- The refusal function moved from `protocol.ts` into the repository module, exported but not from the package entry, under the same name. It is one sentence for all three doors, and `protocol.ts` imports it.
- Before (booted showcase): `PUT /api/v1/meta/object/X?mode=draft` with no `?package=` answered `200 "(env-wide, state=draft)"`. The draft landed in the package whose id sorts first (SQLite's index order), whichever package was saved first. That held in five runs over two package pairs.
- After: `409 RESOURCE_CONFLICT`: "Name the package this save is for, then send it again: ... object 'qa_probe_draft_pq' belongs to 2 packages ('com.qa.p', 'com.qa.q'), and a save that names none has no single row to write." No draft is written. The one-package control still saves into its package.

**3. The delete's `_lock` gate takes the package the delete names**, as the save gate does (`assertLockAllowsDelete` now carries `packageId` through to `getEffectiveLock`).

- Measured: the card's premise is false. A delete naming P is refused when only Q's copy is locked, and the save naming P is refused exactly the same way. That save behavior is pinned since #21803 in `protocol-lock-artifact-package-axis.test.ts` case 1 ("request naming package A ... save refused ITEM_LOCKED").
- The lock is the strictest across every shipping package and every stored row in scope (#21761, #21803). The address only picks whose prose the refusal carries. So the save gate's parity changes the refusal's reason, never its verdict.
- Before: with A and B both shipping `'full'`, a delete naming B carried "Packaged lock of com.example.a.". After: "Packaged lock of com.example.b.", as the save naming B does.
- Admitting `?package=P` when only Q is locked would make the delete door looser than both reads naming P, which report `lock: 'full', deletable: false`. It would also reverse a ruled design, so that question goes to the maintainer through the report, not this PR.

## Where the edits sit

- `packages/metadata-protocol/src/sys-metadata-repository.ts`: `resolveWriteHead` and its docblock, `put`'s refusal, and the moved `packagelessAddressAmbiguityRefusal`.
- `packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts`: `restoreArtifactRegistryView` (a new tier ahead of the retirement tiers), `assertLockAllowsDelete` and its one call site in `deleteMetaItem`. Two more hunks lie outside the claim's declared regions:
  - the `./sys-metadata-repository.js` import line, plus the removal of the moved refusal (formerly around line 1224);
  - one stale comment line in `packagelessAddress`'s docblock ("`resolveWriteHead`, unchanged").

  None overlaps PR #23358's regions or PR #23375's (`eeb95f7ff`, merged in, with no conflict).
- Tests: `protocol.packageless-save-address.test.ts` and `sys-metadata-repository.draft-package-inherit.test.ts` (item 2); `objectql/src/protocol-delete-object-registry-heal.test.ts` (item 1, real `SchemaRegistry`); `objectql/src/protocol-lock-artifact-package-axis.test.ts` (item 3, real `SchemaRegistry`). Each extends an existing file and its existing engine double, so no new double is added.
- Two existing pins follow the change:
  - `protocol.object-registry-write-through-spelling.test.ts`: the `applyRegistryWriteThrough` call-site count goes from 6 to 7. The new caller is traced in the header: it folds through `canonicalMetaType`.
  - `protocol.view-container-reset-expansions.test.ts`: its org-scope case called the heal directly while the published row was still stored. It now removes the row the reset removes before healing, because a still-stored row is now what the heal registers.

## Tests

Every reading below is from `a77f32b92` (the first `main` merge) unless a line says otherwise. The second merge (`ae6b35c16`, PR #23375 and two others) is re-verified in the last bullet.

- Before the fix, the new pins on unmodified code:
  - `metadata-protocol`: 8 failed of 49. These are the two-package draft refusals (both orders, door and repository), `headAt` naming no package (both orders), and the package-less-row-first inheritance. The package-first control and the naming-one-package case passed.
  - `objectql`: 7 failed of 35. These are 4 object cases (tenant and control-plane kernels, both save orders), the dashboard case, and 2 lock-prose cases (delete naming B). Case 4 of the lock suite ("delete naming A is refused as the save naming A is") and the heal CONTROL case passed before the fix.
- After the fix:
  - `pnpm --filter @objectstack/metadata-protocol test`: 235 files passed (3 skipped), 28375 tests passed.
  - `pnpm --filter @objectstack/objectql test`: 414 files, 8083 tests passed, run against rebuilt `metadata-protocol` `dist`.
  - `pnpm --filter @objectstack/rest test`: 281 files, 5845 passed (326 skipped).
  - `pnpm --filter @objectstack/client test`: 51 files, 663 passed.
  - `pnpm --filter @objectstack/metadata-protocol typecheck`: OK. `--listFiles` shows all four changed test files are compiled.
  - `pnpm --filter @objectstack/objectql typecheck` (including `check:test-typecheck`): OK.
- Ablations: each run on a committed fix through `node scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` in wrap mode. The anchor went 1 to 0 and the blob changed. The tool restored the file and proved `blob == HEAD` with an empty `git diff HEAD`.
  - Item 3 (the delete gate drops the package): rebuilt; `ablation-dist-preflight` found the marker in 2 dist files; 2 red (delete naming B under both orders).
  - Item 1 (the remaining-rows tier switched off): rebuilt; marker in dist; 5 red; CONTROL green.
  - Item 2 (`put`'s refusal switched off): source-resolved suites, so no dist step; 4 red (both orders, door and repository).
  - Restore legs: rebuilt, then `--absent` confirmed the marker gone from all 24 dist files with a clean tree. Everything green again: 20 and 15 objectql tests, 49 metadata-protocol tests.
- Gate battery: `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands` with no paths (67 commands) at `a77f32b92`. 66 exit 0, among them `check:adr-0087-registration` (exemption `no-migration-prescription` noted), `check:changeset-no-major`, `check:empty-changeset`, `check:durability-log-level` (89 read seams, none invents an answer), `check:engine-double-contract`, `check:nul-bytes`, `check:test-source-alias` and `check:cross-package-test-inputs`. NOT MEASURED: type-check-debt, reason: it exceeded the 420 s per-gate budget of the local battery (exit 124); CI runs it.
- Merged tree `ae6b35c16` (main with PR #23375, PR #23386 and PR #23384; no conflict, and none touches the edited regions):
  - Re-derived gate list: the same 67 commands; all 67 exit 0. That includes `check:type-check-debt` (re-measure OK, 250.8 s, "none above its recorded number") and the rest of the list above.
  - `dispatch-gates --ran` reconciliation: 67 derived, 67 run, 0 unrun.
  - `pnpm --filter @objectstack/metadata-protocol typecheck`: exit 0.
  - The four suite re-runs (metadata-protocol, objectql, rest, client) are in progress behind the shared verify lock. Their verdicts go in the `os-dev-report` comment on the card, not here.

## Acceptance notes

- Item 1, a visible side effect on objects: after the per-package delete, a read naming the deleted package (`GET /api/v1/meta/object/X?package=P`) now falls through to the registry's entry and serves Q's object with 200, where it answered 404. A boot would produce the same, because the registry holds one object per name.
- Item 2, refusal order: a draft save carrying an `If-Match` taken from a `?package=P` draft read, but sent without `?package=`, meets the `METADATA_CONFLICT` token check before the repository's `RESOURCE_CONFLICT`. Likewise, a permission set whose body names a package meets the owner-binding judge first. Both are refused either way.
- Item 2, flow credentials: a flow draft with an explicit credential stores it in the write-only channel before `put` refuses. That is the channel's documented put-failure behavior.
- Draft receipts: a package-less draft save's receipt still reads "(env-wide, state=draft)" without naming the inherited package.
- Observations read from source and not measured: `rollbackMetaItem` and `restoreVersion` read the active row with no package predicate, as does the legacy raw-engine delete path. These are not filed.
- Measured, not fixed here (reported to the seat as a finding): `DELETE /api/v1/meta/object/qa_probe_drop?package=com.qa.p&dropStorage=true`, on an object whose `com.qa.q` row remains, answered 200 "and it still exists: its row bound to package 'com.qa.q' remains". It still dropped the table: the record created before the delete is gone, `GET /api/v1/data/qa_probe_drop` answers `500 DATABASE_ERROR`, and `POST` answers `404 OBJECT_NOT_FOUND`. `shouldDropStorage` does not ask whether a row of the object remains. Two remedies are possible (skip the drop and say so, or refuse the delete), so it is not a mechanical in-place fix.
- Measured, not fixed here (reported to the seat as a finding): `PUT /api/v1/meta/object/X?package=Q` of a runtime object that package P already owns answers `200 "Saved object 'X' (env-wide, package=Q)"`, while the registry refuses Q's layer: the dev log says `registerObject failed ... is already owned by package "com.qa.p"`, at warn. ADR-0029 D9.9's producer refusal (`OBJECT_OVERLAY_PACKAGE_MISMATCH`) only asks about a packaged (code) owner.
